app/server/api/abilities/[name].get.ts — matching server endpoint, own directory
app/app/components/SiteHeader.vue:10-13 — nav only links Pokémon and Types, no Abilities link to clean up
app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:82-90 — only other reference is the Pokémon page's Abilities section, spec-mandated content in the resource it belongs to
app/server/api/pokemon/[name].get.ts:92-95 — abilities mapping removed with two lines
removability.rationale: Abilities is a self-contained route/endpoint pair; removal is two directory deletions plus the (unavoidable) abilities section on the Pokémon page pair, with no nav or dead-code cleanup beyond two now-unused generic props.

evidence: app/app/composables/usePageData.ts:8-16 — every page's fetch and 404 behavior lives in one composable
app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:22-40 — base URL, caching, 404-on-miss all centralized
app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:125 — card sprite built in cardsFor for move/ability/type lists
app/server/api/pokedex.get.ts:38 — home list re-implements sprite construction with a different id, so the sprite bug needs fixing in two places
app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:51 vs app/app/utils/format.ts:3 — humanize implemented twice (server and app); a change to humanization rules must land in both
changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious server endpoint or helper, but the two card-building paths and the duplicated humanize mean the sprite and naming scenarios each require two coordinated edits.

evidence: app/app/pages/types/[name].vue:2-8, app/app/pages/moves/[name].vue:2-8, app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:4-29 — pages depend only on JSON payload shapes via usePageData, never on server internals
app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:3-7 — components take narrow prop interfaces, no reach into pages
app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:22-47 — server routes depend on one API client, never on each other

app/app/pages/types/[name].vue:2, app/app/pages/moves/[name].vue:4, app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:5, app/app/components/MoveTable.vue:9-11 — TypeRef shape hand-copied into four+ files; server routes return untyped payloads so drift is silent
app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:9 — process.env.API_BASE_URL read directly instead of Nuxt runtimeConfig, bypassing the framework's config seam
coupling.rationale: Loose coupling with clear seams (JSON endpoints, prop-driven components, one fetch composable), dragged down by duplicated types across the app/server boundary and an env read that sidesteps runtimeConfig.

evidence: app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:114-128 — cardsFor stretches across move/ability/type lists via an optional extra() callback instead of flag params; used by 3 routes
app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:3-7 — optional types/note props handle real card variation (home, hidden-ability) without duplication
app/app/components/MoveTable.vue:9-16 — showLevel boolean maps to genuine variation (level-up vs other methods); caption+rows keep it reusable
app/app/components/PageSection.vue:1-14 — section/heading/id pattern collapsed into one component with useId
app/server/api/pokedex.get.ts:30-43 — home endpoint re-implements card construction (sprite + id + sort) instead of reusing cardsFor, the one real copy-paste seam
app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:104-108 — Card type defined server-side but redeclared inline in every page instead of shared/types
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions track the app's real variation well (cardsFor's callback, optional card props, PageSection), with limited copy-paste around the home list's card pipeline and repeatedly redeclared payload types.

findings.issue: Card sprite/id construction is duplicated: the home endpoint builds card objects (sprite: spriteUrl(id), sort by id) independently of cardsFor, and the two would even use different ids under a species/default-Pokémon mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Have /api/pokedex reuse a shared species-card helper (or cardsFor) so sprite, dex-number and ordering logic has one home.

findings.issue: humanize is implemented twice (server/utils/pokeapi.ts:51 and app/utils/format.ts:3); Nuxt 4's shared/utils directory exists precisely for this and auto-imports into both app and server. A rule change (e.g. 'Mr. Mime' handling) must be made twice or display and search behavior diverge.
findings.suggestion: Move humanize (and ideally dexNumber/orDash) into shared/utils/ and delete the two copies.

findings.issue: Every page hand-declares its payload interfaces while the matching server routes return untyped values, so a server change (e.g. renaming a field) silently drifts from the page type; TypeRef alone is copied into 4+ files.
findings.suggestion: Type the server route returns and put shared payload types (Card, TypeRef, TypeBadgeTarget) in shared/types/, importing them in pages and components.

findings.issue: API base URL read from process.env directly rather than Nuxt runtimeConfig (runtimeConfig.apiBase + useRuntimeConfig(event)), bypassing the framework's documented config seam and its .env/test overrides.
findings.suggestion: Define runtimeConfig in nuxt.config.ts and read it inside apiBase().

findings.issue: Games mapping couples gameRecords to the insertion order of a Set by spreading [...gameNames] twice inside the map; adding or reordering entries there is fragile.
findings.suggestion: Materialize const gameList = [...gameNames] once and iterate it for both fetches and labels.

findings.issue: The note prop (and cardsFor's extra callback param) exist only for the hidden-ability case; removing the Abilities feature leaves them unused.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as generic props, but note them for cleanup if Abilities ever goes away.

findings.issue: Search fires router.replace on every keystroke with no debounce; each keystroke also re-runs the full 1025-species matches computed.
findings.suggestion: Debounce the URL sync (~300ms, as the spec permits) while keeping the in-memory search immediate.

summary: This is a well-factored Nuxt 4 app that a team could own: one API client owns the data source and caching, one composable owns page fetching and 404s, and pages/components are thin and prop-driven, so most changes land in a single obvious file. The main editability costs are the duplicated card-sprite pipeline between cardsFor and the home endpoint (the sprite bug scenario needs two fixes), humanize implemented twice across the app/server seam despite Nuxt's shared/ directory, and payload types redeclared per page instead of shared. Removability and data-source changes are close to ideal; the rest is a few findable edits away from single-place fixes.
